title: Cluster-Wide Task Slowdown Detection in Cloud System

problem.claim: Detecting slow tasks matters for cloud operations because slowdowns affect user experience and can cause substantial liquidated damages.

gap.claim: Single-task detection is impractical and inefficient at large cluster scale, and common single-task slowdowns do not necessarily indicate cluster malfunction.

contributions.claim: SORN detects cluster-wide task slowdowns from task-duration distributions, with complexity not dependent on the number of tasks.
SORN includes Skimming Attention for reconstructing compound periodicity and a Neural Optimal Transport module for distinguishing cluster-wide slowdowns from other exceptional fluctuations.
A picky loss function adaptively assigns higher weights to reliable training-set time slots when anomalies are present.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report empirical and theoretical analysis of a flaw in standard attention for reconstructing low-amplitude subperiods under compound periodicity.
The authors report extensive experiments showing that SORN outperforms state-of-the-art methods on multiple real-world industrial datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Slow task detection is important because it affects user experience and financial liability.
Single-task detection is inadequate for millions of concurrent tasks and may confuse ordinary virtual-environment fluctuations with cluster malfunction.
The work shifts to cluster-wide slowdown detection using task-duration distributions.
The authors identify a standard-attention limitation for low-amplitude subperiod reconstruction in compound periodicity.
SORN combines Skimming Attention, Neural Optimal Transport, and picky loss; the authors report superior results on multiple industrial datasets.
